title: OPTIMA 79: Geometry in model-based algorithms for derivative-free unconstrained optimization (feature article)
contribution: Single-author expository essay (OPTIMA 79, May 2009) that states, in Scheinberg's own words, the minimal-geometry position of model-based DFO: sample-set geometry is necessary for convergence (shown by a hand-checkable counterexample on the Fasano-Nocedal-Morales geometry-free method), but extra sample points are needed only when the model gradient becomes small, thanks to the self-correcting property of the trust-region framework (Scheinberg-Toint algorithm).
problem_entry: Theory-practice gap: the CSV convergence theory strongly depends on model-improvement steps, while the geometry-free Fasano-Nocedal-Morales code was 'least wasteful' with 'quite encouraging' results; asked outright whether geometry matters (pp. 3-4).
key_idea: A failed trust-region step implies a large model error, which by the Lagrange error bound (3.3) implies a far point or a large |l_j(x+)|, so swapping in x+ repairs geometry for free; dedicated geometry work is confined to a criticality step with a shrinking threshold (pp. 4-5).
assumptions: Unconstrained, Lipschitz gradient, derivatives unavailable or too costly, exact f (noise only as motivation), poised set with Lambda > 1; convergence 'under the usual and reasonable conditions' left unspecified (pp. 1-5).
proof_devices: Lagrange representation m(x)=sum f(y_j) l_j(x) and error bound |m-f| <= M sum ||y_j-x||^{d+1}|l_j(x)| (3.2)-(3.3), p. 2
Lambda-poisedness and finite-termination swap lemma (Lemma 3.3), p. 2
fully-linear / fully-quadratic model abstraction with a finite certify-or-construct requirement, p. 3
Cauchy decrease condition as the only step requirement, p. 3
hand-checkable 2-D counterexample: six points around (10,0), model degenerates to x1^2, stops at (0,0) where grad f = (0,10*alpha), p. 4
contrapositive reading of the error bound: unsuccessful step => far point or large Lagrange value => improving swap (self-correction), p. 4
order-independence of the counterexample => criticality step is the irreducible safeguard, p. 5
cost-accounting argument: Lagrange-polynomial upkeep costs the same as model upkeep, p. 5
experiments: none of her own; Fasano et al. results reported only qualitatively, with the caveat that they used full quadratic models; Figure 1 only illustrates the counterexample (pp. 4-5).
positioning: History told along the geometry axis (Nelder-Mead adapts and collapses; pattern search fixes shape, gains convergence, loses curvature; model-based methods must maintain geometry); credits then refutes Fasano-Nocedal-Morales; presents the new algorithm as the closest convergent algorithm to NEWUOA and DFO; Moré-Wild not cited (pp. 1-6).
writing: Question-driven section titles, a necessary-however-not-necessary-unless contribution sentence, intuition paragraph before the algorithm with rigour delegated to [20], abstraction before instantiation, light hedging, zero proofs, some newsletter-level typos (pp. 1-5).
limits_future: Only a first-order limit-point result; 'It remains to be seen' whether stronger theory holds; no numerics for the new algorithm; noise and constraints untreated; why inaccurate quadratic models work is left to Nocedal's column (pp. 1-5).

method_links.note: Stated, first person: geometry necessary; extra points only when model gradient small; criticality step irreducible; Lagrange bookkeeping at no extra cost. Say-do consistent with S030 (c01). Correction: the Moré-Wild framing and 'only minimal quality controls' wording in SKILL.md are Nocedal's (column, p. 6), not Scheinberg's; title now verified; she was co-editor of Optima (p. 10).
Self-correction credited to the trust-region framework; new algorithm differs from the CSV framework only in Steps 1, 4b and 5; closeness to practical codes offered as merit.

Deterministic precursor of the oracle contract: fully-linear models tie gradient error to kappa_eg*Delta on the ball, and the algorithm only needs a finite certify-or-construct procedure; no probability yet (BSV 2014 later makes it probabilistic).

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Stated form: credits the geometry-free code's efficiency and results, asks whether geometry matters, answers with a counterexample plus the self-correcting mechanism and an algorithm that pays for geometry only at criticality; practiced form in S030 (c01).

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: closest convergent relative of the practical code
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: New algorithm sold as the closest theoretically convergent algorithm to NEWUOA and DFO; SKILL.md reports the same framing for the 2026 Powell-style preprint.

transferable: Tell the field's history along one design axis (here sample-set geometry) so each prior method is a success and a failure on that axis and your contribution is the next point (pp. 1-2).
Write the algorithm against an abstract quality property (fully linear: ||grad f - grad m|| <= kappa_eg*Delta on the ball) plus a finite certify-or-construct requirement, then instantiate (p. 3).
Read the error bound backwards: failed step => large error => large controllable quantity => a free repair move (p. 4).

Hand-checkable 2-D counterexample, non-stationarity verified by direct differentiation, plus an argument that the outcome is independent of the replacement rule, which isolates the irreducible safeguard (pp. 4-5).
Answer a cost objection by showing the added bookkeeping costs the same as the model update, so per-iteration cost matches the heuristic competitor except on rare criticality iterations (p. 5).
Credit a competitor's efficiency before refuting its guarantee, and name what its experiments relied on (full quadratic models) (p. 4).
One contribution sentence pairing necessity with minimal sufficiency: X is necessary for G; however, X is not needed unless Y (p. 4).
coauthors: none (single author); issue co-edited with A. Caprara under editor A. Lodi

quotes.text: it turns out that it is not necessary to compute extra sample points unless the gradient of the model becomes small.
We also note that in fact this new algorithm is the closest theoretically convergent algorithm to the practical implementations in [19] and [6] that exist so far.
